## Overview

`docs/features/tool_calling.md` says named function calling works "by default", and that `tool_choice="required"` "is enabled by default and will work with any supported model". Since #30613 (first released in v0.14.0), both return HTTP 400 unless the server has loaded a tool parser, and the server loads one only when `--enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--tool-call-parser` are both set. This PR updates the Named and Required Function Calling sections and the `--enable-auto-tool-choice` entry to match. Related: #55754, #55762.

## Claims

- Named and Required Function Calling state that both flags are needed and that a request without a loaded parser returns HTTP 400. They also note that this check does not reject requests to models in the official Mistral format or to gpt-oss models.
- Both sections now point to [Constrained Decoding Behavior](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/docs/features/tool_calling.md#L112-L125) for how far the arguments follow the tool's schema, instead of saying the output strictly matches it. That later section enforces a tool's schema under a structural tag only when the tool sets `strict: true` or the server uses `--tool-strict-level parameter`.
- The `--enable-auto-tool-choice` entry under Automatic Function Calling says that named and required function calling also need it.
- The sentence that alternative decoding backends are on the V1 roadmap is removed; [`docs/usage/v1_guide.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/docs/usage/v1_guide.md#L157) lists them as functional.

## Validation

The behaviour described comes from the code at the base commit `6d01893`:

- [`OnlineRenderer.render_chat()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L263-L290): with no tool parser, and neither a Mistral tokenizer nor gpt-oss, `"auto"` fails with `"auto" tool choice requires --enable-auto-tool-choice and --tool-call-parser to be set`, and `"required"` or a named choice fails with `tool_choice=... requires --tool-call-parser to be set`. Both are 400 `BadRequestError`.
- [`ParserManager.get_tool_parser()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/vllm/parser/parser_manager.py#L33-L35) returns `None` when `enable_auto_tools` is false, so `--tool-call-parser` alone loads no parser. #55754 reproduces this over HTTP with `--tool-call-parser hermes`.
- [`test_tool_choice_validation_without_parser`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6d018934838a0c8c6beed244aa1ca327e1ed7182/tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py#L2866) covers the case with no parser.

Driving `OnlineRenderer.render_chat()` from the v0.32.0 wheel on CPU, with the Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct tokenizer and no engine, gives the same result. With no tool flags, and with `--tool-call-parser hermes` alone, a request with tools returns 400 for `tool_choice` omitted, `"auto"`, `"required"` and named; with both flags all four are accepted. The check and `get_tool_parser()` are the same in v0.32.0 and at the base commit.

`pre-commit run --files docs/features/tool_calling.md` passes, including `markdownlint-cli2` and `typos`. A local `mkdocs build` did not get past `docs/mkdocs/gen_files/generate_argparse.py`, which imports modules that need the compiled CUDA extensions, so the Read the Docs preview is the render check.

## Details

The 400 is intended. #30613 added it because, without the two flags, these requests "would silently degrade instead of returning a clear error". The docs predate it. Up to v0.11.0 the JSON schema for a named or required call was built in `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params()` without a parser; #27383 (v0.11.1) moved that into the tool parser.

#55762 proposes loading the configured parser without `--enable-auto-tool-choice` for named and required choices. If it lands, the sentences that name both flags should say that `--tool-call-parser` is enough; that PR does not change the docs. No open PR edits these sections. #60585 adds an Allowed Tools section right after Required Function Calling, next to a line this PR changes, so the second of the two to merge may need a rebase.

This PR leaves out two related points. The error message names only `--tool-call-parser`, but it sits in the validation block that #55762 rewrites. The Responses API does not apply this check (#39221), and the new sentences describe the chat completion API.

This PR was prepared with the help of a coding agent.

@@ -85,10 +85,10 @@ For more advanced usage, including parallel tool calls and different model-speci
 
 ## Named Function Calling
 
-vLLM supports named function calling in the chat completion API by default. This should work with most structured outputs backends supported by vLLM. You are guaranteed a validly-parsable function call - not a
-high-quality one. On recent Mistral models in the official Mistral format, a call is not guaranteed; see [Mistral Models](#mistral-models-mistral).
+vLLM supports named function calling in the chat completion API when the server runs a tool parser. Start the server with both `--enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--tool-call-parser`. vLLM loads the parser named by `--tool-call-parser` only when `--enable-auto-tool-choice` is also set. Without a loaded parser, a request with a named `tool_choice` returns HTTP 400. Requests to models in the official Mistral format and to gpt-oss models are not rejected by this check.
+
+The function call is constrained with structured outputs. This should work with most structured outputs backends supported by vLLM. You are guaranteed a validly-parsable function call - not a high-quality one. How far the arguments are held to the tool's parameter schema depends on the parser and on the tool's `strict` field; see [Constrained Decoding Behavior](#constrained-decoding-behavior). On recent Mistral models in the official Mistral format, a call is not guaranteed; see [Mistral Models](#mistral-models-mistral).
 
-vLLM will use structured outputs to ensure the response matches the tool parameter object defined by the JSON schema in the `tools` parameter.
 For best results, we recommend ensuring that the expected output format / schema is specified in the prompt to ensure that the model's intended generation is aligned with the schema that it's being forced to generate by the structured outputs backend.
 
 To use a named function, you need to define the functions in the `tools` parameter of the chat completion request, and
@@ -98,9 +98,9 @@ In the Responses API, `tool_choice={"type": "function", "name": "..."}` can sele
 
 ## Required Function Calling
 
-vLLM supports the `tool_choice='required'` option in the chat completion API. Similar to the named function calling, it also uses structured outputs, so this is enabled by default and will work with any supported model. However, support for alternative decoding backends are on the [roadmap](../usage/v1_guide.md#features) for the V1 engine.
+vLLM supports the `tool_choice='required'` option in the chat completion API. Like named function calling, it uses structured outputs and needs a tool parser, with the same server flags and the same exceptions. Without a loaded parser, a request with `tool_choice='required'` returns HTTP 400.
 
-When tool_choice='required' is set, the model is guaranteed to generate one or more tool calls based on the specified tool list in the `tools` parameter. The number of tool calls depends on the user's query. The output format strictly follows the schema defined in the `tools` parameter. On recent Mistral models in the official Mistral format, a call is not guaranteed; see [Mistral Models](#mistral-models-mistral).
+When tool_choice='required' is set, the model is guaranteed to generate one or more tool calls based on the specified tool list in the `tools` parameter. The number of tool calls depends on the user's query. The output follows the schema defined in the `tools` parameter as described in [Constrained Decoding Behavior](#constrained-decoding-behavior). On recent Mistral models in the official Mistral format, a call is not guaranteed; see [Mistral Models](#mistral-models-mistral).
 
 ## None Function Calling
 
@@ -163,7 +163,7 @@ The floor never relaxes a constraint the request would already receive: tools th
 To enable this feature, you should set the following flags:
 
 * `--enable-auto-tool-choice` -- **mandatory** Auto tool choice. It tells vLLM that you want to enable the model to generate its own tool calls when it
-deems appropriate.
+deems appropriate. vLLM loads the tool parser selected by `--tool-call-parser` only when this flag is set, so [named](#named-function-calling) and [required](#required-function-calling) function calling also need it.
 * `--tool-call-parser` -- select the tool parser to use (listed below). Additional tool parsers
 will continue to be added in the future. You can also register your own tool parsers in the `--tool-parser-plugin`.
 * `--tool-parser-plugin` -- **optional** tool parser plugin used to register user defined tool parsers into vllm, the registered tool parser name can be specified in `--tool-call-parser`.
